newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Swedish debt yields could not hold on to morning gains and ended the session higher on Monday.
The crown strengthened at first but buyers of marks stepped in just below the 4.50 crown level versus the mark.

The focus was on the FOMC meeting which starts on Tuesday at which the market expected a hike of 25 basis points. Some dealers said the crown would firm if the hike was more than 25 basis points, while other dealers said the opposite.
"If the Fed hikes by more than 25 basis points, people could start selling U.S. securities and stock which will soften the dollar and that could spill over to the crown," one said.
The crown softened to 4.5220 crowns to the mark versus 4.5190 late on Friday.
Yields were pushed up by rising Finnish yields although many players were sidelined ahead of the FOMC meeting.
Six month T-bill rate rose five basis points to 4.27 percent and the ten year bond yield increased by five basis points to 7.42 percent.
The Riksbank will hold a repo tender on Tuesday but the market was not expecting a cut from the current 4.10 percent.
